prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a check to reject an already in-flight request id, but #3063 keys the check on the existing `str(message.id)` routing key, which collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key — so it can falsely 409 a distinct id or still cross-wire responses between an int/string id pair, and a string id equal to `_GET_stream` can collide with the reserved GET-stream slot. #3221 replaces the key scheme with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that fixes both edge cases while implementing the same duplicate-id rejection, so it's a strict superset fix for the same root cause.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change the same conditional in pre_parse_json to stop pre-parsing for union-with-str annotations, but they draw the line differently. #2032 skips pre-parsing whenever every union member is in a fixed set {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}; that also disables pre-parsing for unions like `str | int`, where json-decoding a numeric string was previously the intended coercion path, not a corruption case. #2032's membership check also doesn't unwrap `Annotated`, so a union member written as `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` isn't recognized as simple and the original corruption bug still reproduces for that (common, description-annotated) form. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` and only disables pre-parsing when no union member other than `str` could ever be produced by decoding JSON (currently `str | None`), so it fixes the reported corruption case, including the Annotated-wrapped-member case, without changing behavior for unions where pre-parsing already yields a correct, intended value.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a check to reject an already in-flight request id, but #3063 keys the check on the existing `str(message.id)` routing key, which collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key — so it can falsely 409 a distinct id or still cross-wire responses between an int/string id pair, and a string id equal to `_GET_stream` can collide with the reserved GET-stream slot. #3221 replaces the key scheme with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that fixes both edge cases while implementing the same duplicate-id rejection, so it's a strict superset fix for the same root cause.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change the same conditional in pre_parse_json to stop pre-parsing for union-with-str annotations, but they draw the line differently. #2032 skips pre-parsing whenever every union member is in a fixed set {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}; that also disables pre-parsing for unions like `str | int`, where json-decoding a numeric string was previously the intended coercion path, not a corruption case. #2032's membership check also doesn't unwrap `Annotated`, so a union member written as `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` isn't recognized as simple and the original corruption bug still reproduces for that (common, description-annotated) form. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` and only disables pre-parsing when no union member other than `str` could ever be produced by decoding JSON (currently `str | None`), so it fixes the reported corruption case, including the Annotated-wrapped-member case, without changing behavior for unions where pre-parsing already yields a correct, intended value.

clusters.pick_reason: #2253 delivers the complete mechanism across both files: it adds the loop in terminate() that closes every writer in _sse_stream_writers, and it changes streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan to call terminate() on active sessions before cancelling the task group — that ordering is what actually makes shutdown graceful. #3218 only registers the GET/standalone SSE writer into _sse_stream_writers (and pops it in the writer's finally block); it never touches streamable_http_manager.py's shutdown sequencing, so by itself it doesn't establish the termination-before-cancel order the fix depends on — it reads as a narrower complement covering the GET path rather than an independent fix for the shutdown problem.

members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py sends the wrong thing when a request is cancelled — it emits an error response for cancellation instead of following spec. Both PRs are based on the identical pre-change blob (243eef5ae6) and rewrite the same cancel() method (lines ~141-158): #2493 removes the erroneous 'send an error response' code and updates the corresponding _handle_request comment/log in server.py to reflect that receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request. #2514 rewrites the same method to instead send a proper notifications/cancelled message (imports CancelledNotificationParams) covering request-timeout and caller-initiated cancellation, and its pragma:no-cover removal on the adjacent RuntimeError check indicates added test coverage for this path. Since both touch the identical original lines of the same method, merging one first will produce a conflict against the other, and #2514 is a superset fix (it not only stops the incorrect response but also implements the spec-correct notifications/cancelled behavior for cases #2493 doesn't add anything for), so they address one root cause.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a check to reject an already in-flight request id, but #3063 keys the check on the existing `str(message.id)` routing key, which collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key — so it can falsely 409 a distinct id or still cross-wire responses between an int/string id pair, and a string id equal to `_GET_stream` can collide with the reserved GET-stream slot. #3221 replaces the key scheme with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that fixes both edge cases while implementing the same duplicate-id rejection, so it's a strict superset fix for the same root cause.
